considered_not_added.reason: not claimed as planets: 37-49 d is the rotation region; the long periods are attributed to an activity cycle or instrument offsets 'or' a long-period planet, with no candidate named (Lalitha et al. 2019, A&A 627, A116; read via WebSearch summary only).

considered_not_added.name: VB 10 b (vB 10 b)
considered_not_added.reason: refuted: the Pravdo & Shaklan 2009 astrometric planet around HD 180617 B (vB 10) was ruled out by precise RVs and astrometry (Bean et al. 2010; Anglada-Escude et al. 2010; Lazorenko et al. 2011), as summarised in Kaminski et al. 2018 Sect. 2. exoplanet.eu still lists it as 'Candidate' with the Bean et al. non-detection remark.

considered_not_added.name: HD 180617 residual signals at ~184-196 d and ~45-50 d
considered_not_added.reason: not claimed as planets; ~46 d is rotation and ~196 d appears in H-alpha, attributed to activity (Kaminski et al. 2018 Sects. 4-5).

considered_not_added.name: GJ 463 residual peaks at 74.0, 8.2 and 15.1 d
considered_not_added.reason: non-significant (FAP >1-10%, Delta lnZ < 0 when modelled); not claimed (Morales et al. 2025 Sect. 5.3).

considered_not_added.name: GJ 680 b / GJ 680 B
considered_not_added.reason: not a planet or brown dwarf: a 0.178 Msun low-mass star (Philipot et al. 2023). Already on the confirmed tab, so not a candidate; see incidental_finds.

incidental_finds_outside_my_scope.item: GJ 680 b (confirmed tab row 522, 7977 Mearth, flagged '>13 MJ - likely BD') is a star, not a brown dwarf: Philipot et al. 2023 (A&A 678, A107), combining HARPS RVs, Hipparcos-Gaia absolute astrometry and NACO relative astrometry (imaged 2005 and 2007), find a = 32 +9/-6 au and a true mass of 0.178 +/- 0.004 Msun (186 +/- 4 MJup), and list GJ 680 B among 'five companions previously reported as brown dwarfs [that] are indeed low-mass stars' (Sect. 5, Table C.3). Feng et al. 2022's 25 MJup / 10.1 au solution is superseded. NASA pscomppars still carries 'GJ 680 b' from Feng+2022. Suggest moving it to the Multi-stars tab as GJ 680 B.

Systems-tab distances for all 20 B13 systems agree with Gaia DR3 parallaxes to within 0.6% (largest: TOI-1231 sheet 90.09 ly vs 89.63 ly from 36.3896 mas, +0.51%; GJ 3341 77.03 vs 76.74 ly, +0.38%). No mismatch over 2%.

exoplanet.eu labels three weak or unrecovered signals in this batch 'Confirmed': GJ 176 c, GJ 649 c and GJ 480 c. NASA lists none of them. The writer should not take exoplanet.eu's status at face value for these.
